0.content: In the temple at Amsvartnir (the Royal Court of the Seelie), a lady who had lost her name and memory was visited by a wolf from the north. She called him a stupid dog, patted his fur and named him Boreas, "North Wind". Without meaning to, her company gave him human speech, wisdom and a god's power. He called her Mother and asked leave to go south. She let him go and called his name one last time. The ancient handwriting at Amsvartnir records this (world quest Echoes of a Forsaken Song, 6.3).

1.content: Boreas came south and warred on Decarabian, God of Storms, while Decarabian walled Old Mondstadt in with gales. Item texts say Boreas could not scratch the Lord of the Tower. After the people rebelled with the wind spirit and Decarabian fell, Boreas decided he was unworthy to become the Anemo Archon, because he could not picture how to bring humanity happiness. He trusted them to the new god and returned north.

2.content: The Knight of Boreas is a human recognised by Boreas as his intermediary with humankind. Known holders: the Wandering Knight, Ravenwood, Rostam and Varka. Few were truly recognised by Boreas himself. The lineage nearly ended twice: at its start, when the first knight left no heir, and five hundred years ago after Rostam died, when Roland left to pursue obsession. Knights usually become Master or Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.

3.content: Varka, the current Knight of Boreas, won the wolf's regard by challenging him many times. When he saw a calamity in the north, he consulted Boreas, who agreed to split his soul and pass a token through Varka's sword. In Nod-Krai, Varka let Roland's shadow "kill" him and so reached the heart of the wolf to meet the corrupted half; he had carried Boreas' thoughts in his own heart, letting the wolf's soul assimilate it ("You get the wolf to swallow the heart").

4.content: Razor lives among the wolves of Wolvendom and calls them his lupical (his family). When riftwolves attacked Springvale, the villagers blamed the wolves and Razor. Boreas appeared and tested Razor and the Traveler. Satisfied, he said Razor spoke the truth and told him to stay out of the pack-on-pack battle, because he was a human, not a wolf. He called the Traveler "Razor's Lupical amongst humans" and later addresses the Traveler as "Human Lupical". Later he agreed that the dark wolves were a world matter, and his pack fought them beside Razor.

5.content: A nameless knight stumbled into Boreas' sleeping palace in the north, seeking relief from the cold, as the wolf himself once did at the Seelie Hall. Boreas agreed to join his journey south to the land he had forgotten. The knight's name was lost; he refused to join the Knights of Favonius, and left no heir. His weapon was Wolf's Gravestone. Jean says he was as free as the wind.

6.content: Wolvendom is a dark forest in the Windwail Highland and the home of Boreas and his wolves. The Temple of the Wolf, near the Thousand Winds Temple, was once used to worship him but is abandoned. Orphans and abandoned young are taken into his pack. Mondstadters see his wolves as shadows and howls: humans rarely meet a wolf's gaze, as Lupus Boreas laid down for his race.

7.comment: Andrius: The Nod-Krai Remnant and the Wild Hunt
7.content: The part of Boreas left in Nod-Krai lay slumbering by a lake. The Abyss, through a shadow of Roland, bent it into leading the Wild Hunt. The Hunt followed his trail across the Ley Lines to strike Wolvendom as well. Venti said the root of the turmoil lay in the remnant that Andrius left in Nod-Krai. Varka went in, met the shadow of Roland and reached the heart of the wolf, where the corrupted half agreed to return to the Ley Lines.

key: In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow
8.content: At Wolvendom, with Boreas' leave, Venti told the wolf's story as a ballad, "In Pursuit of Wind and Shadow", in which the aging Boreas turns to the God of Anemo and says, "So, this is the world the humans dreamed of." The bard framed it as the wolf's gift to the world, not a tragedy. Boreas did not add to the telling.

9.comment: Andrius: Dvalin and the Four Winds
9.content: Boreas is the Wolf of the North, one of the Four Winds that Barbatos founded when the Knights of Favonius were formed a thousand years ago. Dvalin is the Dragon of the East. In 6.4 Boreas senses the East Wind's presence when Venti calls on Dvalin, who flies the Traveler to Nod-Krai and says the Knight of Boreas awaits below.

10.content: Because a human heart cannot bear a wolf's soul without being devoured, Boreas lends his power to weapons instead. The Wolf's Gravestone belonged to the first Knight of Boreas. Razor carries a Ferrous Shadow, a design modelled on Ravenwood's greatsword; Gest of the Mighty Wolf is said to have been forged by Ravenwood. The Favonius Sword was Rostam's. Venti recites an old song about this: a weapon of common iron becomes divine through friendship between man and wolf.

key: Wolf of the North weekly boss
11.comment: Andrius: Wolf of the North Challenge
11.content: Gameplay: after Razor's quest, players can fight the wolf in his Wolvendom arena; the introduction says "Traveler... Ready to test your skills?" His immunity to Cryo and Anemo and the drops (Tail of Boreas, Ring of Boreas, Spirit Locket of Boreas) are game mechanics. The item texts describe his power in-world: the form is made of ice and wind and cannot hold all of it.
